mainTopic: Suffering and forgiveness: burying children, יסורין של אהבה, stories of sick sages and רב הונא's loss, and אבא בנימין's teachings on prayer and the bed.
overview: The amud opens by finishing a teaching that one who learns תורה, does גמילות חסדים, and buries his children has all his sins forgiven. An elder gives the source for the last item with a גזירה שוה on the word עון. רבי יוחנן then rules that נגעים and suffering through children are not יסורין של אהבה. The גמרא defends both parts of his rule against challenges. Next come three stories of sick sages who want neither their suffering nor its reward and are healed by a friend's hand, because a prisoner cannot free himself. In the story of רב הונא, his wine turns to vinegar, he examines his deeds, fixes how he treats his sharecropper, and his loss is restored. The amud ends with teachings of אבא בנימין: praying right after getting out of bed (רש״י's reading of 'close to my bed'), placing one's bed between north and south, and the punishment for leaving a friend alone while he prays. The question of the reward for waiting is answered on the next amud.

steps.title: Burying one's children brings forgiveness
steps.stepSummary: The end of the statement from the previous lines: one who also buries his children has all his sins forgiven.
steps.simpleTranslation: …and one who buries his children has all his sins forgiven.
steps.whatsHappening: We are joining a statement that began on the previous lines. It finishes by saying that a person who learns תורה, does חסד, and buries his children is forgiven for all his sins.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The full statement lists three things: learning תורה, doing גמילות חסדים, and burying one's children. Together they bring complete forgiveness. Only the last item appears here, and it is the one the גמרא will question next.

keyTerms.meaning: Buries his children, meaning a parent whose children died during his lifetime
They forgive him; his sins are pardoned

phrases.english: and buries his sons —
all his sins are forgiven for him.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְקוֹבֵר אֶת בָּנָיו מוֹחֲלִין לוֹ עַל כׇּל עֲוֹנוֹתָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the statement that began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Learning תורה, doing גמילות חסדים, and burying one's children together bring forgiveness of all sins.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן asks for the source about burying children
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן shows that תורה and חסד are hinted at in a פסוק. He then asks where we learn that burying children brings forgiveness.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said to him: I understand the parts about תורה and חסד, because it is written, "With חסד and אמת, sin is forgiven." חסד means acts of kindness, as it says, "One who pursues צדקה and חסד finds life, צדקה, and honor." אמת means תורה, as it says, "Buy truth and do not sell it." But where do we learn this about one who buries his children?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן agrees that two of the three items have a clear source in a פסוק. He asks for a source for the third item, burying one's children.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof uses one פסוק that promises forgiveness for חסד and אמת. Two more פסוקים show that חסד means גמילות חסדים and אמת means תורה. Nothing in these פסוקים mentions children, so the third item still needs a source.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense; I can accept this part (the next word, אֶלָּא, brings the problem)
Sin is forgiven, or atoned for
From where do we know this? A request for a source

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said to him:
It makes sense for Torah and acts of kindness,
as it is written: "With kindness and truth, sin is atoned for."
phrases.notes: משלי 16:6

phrases.english: "Kindness" means acts of kindness,
as it is said: "One who pursues charity and kindness
will find life, charity, and honor."
phrases.notes: משלי 21:21. חסד appears right next to צדקה, so it means acts of kindness.

phrases.english: "Truth" means Torah,
as it is said: "Buy truth and do not sell it."
phrases.notes: משלי 23:23

phrases.english: But "one who buries his sons" — from where do we know it?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא תּוֹרָה וּגְמִילוּת חֲסָדִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts two of the three items from step 1 and asks for a source for the third.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source in a פסוק showing that burying one's children brings forgiveness of sins.

steps.title: An elder gives the source through the word עון
steps.stepSummary: An elder, quoting רבי שמעון בן יוחאי, links two פסוקים that both use the word עון. This shows that burying children also brings forgiveness.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain elder taught him in the name of רבי שמעון בן יוחאי: We learn it from the word "עון" appearing in two places. Here it is written, "With חסד and אמת, sin is atoned for," and there it is written, "He repays the sin of the fathers into the lap of their children."
steps.whatsHappening: An elder answers רבי יוחנן's question with a גזירה שוה, a link between two פסוקים that share the same word. Both פסוקים use the word עון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first פסוק says עון is atoned for. The second פסוק says the עון of the fathers is paid back through their children. Because the same word appears in both, the forgiveness from the first פסוק also applies when the father suffers through his children.

keyTerms.meaning: A certain elder whose name is not given
It is learned from the word עון appearing in both places; this kind of link is called a גְּזֵרָה שָׁוָה
Here / there: the two פסוקים being linked

steps.whatToRemember: The source for forgiveness through burying children is a גזירה שוה on the word עון. משלי 16:6 promises that sin is atoned for, and ירמיהו 32:18 shows the father's sin being paid back through his children.

phrases.english: A certain elder taught him,
in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai:
It is derived from "sin" and "sin."
phrases.notes: The same word appears in two פסוקים, so we connect them. This is a גזירה שוה.

phrases.english: It is written here: "With kindness and truth, sin is atoned for,"
and it is written there: "And He repays the sin of the fathers
into the lap of their children."
phrases.notes: ירמיהו 32:18

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנָא לֵיהּ הַהוּא סָבָא מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 2's request for a source.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גזירה שוה on the word עון links forgiveness of sin to the father's sin being paid back through his children.

steps.title: Leprosy and suffering through children are not afflictions of love
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן rules that נגעים and suffering through children do not count as יסורין של אהבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: נגעים and children are not afflictions of love.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן starts a new idea. He names two kinds of suffering that are not counted as יסורין של אהבה, the loving suffering that God brings on a person without sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He picks out two specific kinds of suffering, נגעים and suffering through children. He says they do not belong in the category of afflictions of love. The previous step just said that burying children brings forgiveness, so this statement sets up a question for the coming lines.

keyTerms.meaning: Afflictions of love: suffering that comes from God's love, not as punishment

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two ideas. Step 3 said burying children brings forgiveness. Here רבי יוחנן says suffering through children is still not counted as an affliction of love. These are two different questions.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
Leprous afflictions and children —
phrases.notes: "Children" here means the pain a person goes through with his children, like losing them.

phrases.english: are not afflictions of love.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן נְגָעִים וּבָנִים אֵינָן יִסּוּרִין שֶׁל אַהֲבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new teaching about which kinds of suffering count as afflictions of love.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: נגעים and suffering through children are not counted as יסורין של אהבה.

steps.title: A ברייתא seems to show that נגעים are a good kind of suffering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן: a ברייתא says the four kinds of נגעים are a מזבח כפרה, so how can he say they are not יסורין של אהבה?
steps.simpleTranslation: And are נגעים really not יסורין של אהבה? But we learned in a ברייתא: anyone who has one of these four kinds of נגעים, they are nothing but an altar of atonement!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions רבי יוחנן's rule from Step 4 by quoting a ברייתא that speaks very positively about נגעים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן said נגעים are not יסורין של אהבה. The ברייתא says נגעים work like a מזבח כפרה, wiping away sins the way a קרבן does. If נגעים are that precious, it seems they should count as יסורין של אהבה.

keyTerms.meaning: Skin afflictions described in ויקרא פרק יג (often called 'leprosy')
The different kinds or colors of נגעים
An 'altar of atonement'. Something that brings כפרה like a קרבן

phrases.english: And are נגעים not [יסורין של אהבה]?
phrases.notes: This points back to רבי יוחנן's rule in Step 4.

phrases.english: But didn't we learn in a ברייתא:
Anyone who has on him
one of these four kinds of נגעים,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 13

phrases.english: they are nothing but an altar of atonement!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּנְגָעִים לָא? וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יוחנן's rule in Step 4 that נגעים are not יסורין של אהבה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's statement that נגעים are not יסורין של אהבה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא calls נגעים a מזבח כפרה. Something that holy and precious seems to be exactly what יסורין של אהבה means.

steps.title: נגעים bring atonement but are still not suffering of love
steps.stepSummary: The first answer: נגעים are a מזבח כפרה, but that does not make them יסורין של אהבה. These are two different things.
steps.simpleTranslation: They are an altar of atonement, but they are not יסורין של אהבה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by saying the ברייתא and רבי יוחנן are talking about two different qualities.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא only says נגעים bring כפרה. It does not say they are יסורין של אהבה. Suffering can wipe away sins without being the special 'suffering of love' that רבי יוחנן was defining, so there is no contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Suffering of love'. A special kind of suffering sent out of ה׳'s love

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think that anything that brings כפרה is automatically יסורין של אהבה. The גמרא here separates the two ideas.

phrases.english: An altar of atonement, they are;
suffering of love, they are not.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִזְבַּח כַּפָּרָה הָווּ, יִסּוּרִין שֶׁל אַהֲבָה לָא הָווּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 5 by separating כפרה from יסורין של אהבה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing two categories: atonement versus suffering of love
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought that if נגעים bring כפרה, they must be יסורין של אהבה.
steps.terutzMaskana: נגעים do bring כפרה, but that is a separate matter. They are still not יסורין של אהבה, as רבי יוחנן said.

steps.title: Second answer: one source is about בבל, the other about ארץ ישראל
steps.stepSummary: Another answer: the ברייתא (נגעים are good suffering) is about 'us' in בבל, and רבי יוחנן (they are not) is about 'them' in ארץ ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say instead: this one is for us, and that one is for them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different answer. Each source is talking about a different place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer accepts that the ברייתא really does treat נגעים as good suffering. The difference depends on how hard life is for a מצורע. In ארץ ישראל people are very careful with טומאה, so a מצורע is sent away from everyone and suffers greatly. In בבל, where people are less careful about this, his suffering is lighter.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And if you want, say instead'. This introduces another possible answer
'For us', meaning the חכמים of בבל
'For them', meaning the people of ארץ ישראל

phrases.english: And if you want, say instead:
This one is for us, and that one is for them.
phrases.notes: 'This one' is the ברייתא, for us in בבל. 'That one' is רבי יוחנן, for them in ארץ ישראל.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי בָּעֵית אֵימָא: הָא לָן, וְהָא לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second, independent answer to the challenge of Step 5.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא and רבי יוחנן seemed to be talking about the same situation.
steps.terutzMaskana: In בבל, נגעים can be good suffering. In ארץ ישראל, where a מצורע is sent away, they are not יסורין של אהבה.

steps.title: Third answer: hidden נגעים versus visible נגעים
steps.stepSummary: A third answer: the ברייתא is about נגעים in hidden places on the body, and רבי יוחנן is about נגעים that people can see.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say instead: this one is about hidden ones, and that one is about public ones.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives one more answer. It splits the two sources by where the נגע appears on the body.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A hidden נגע does not embarrass the person or push others away, so it can be יסורין של אהבה, as the ברייתא says. A visible נגע makes people keep away from him. That is the kind רבי יוחנן says is not יסורין של אהבה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'In private'. Here it means a נגע on a hidden part of the body
'In public'. Here it means a נגע on a part of the body people can see

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן's rule that נגעים are not יסורין של אהבה survives the challenge, with three possible answers: (1) כפרה is different from יסורין של אהבה; (2) בבל versus ארץ ישראל; (3) hidden versus visible נגעים.

phrases.english: And if you want, say instead:
This one is about hidden ones, that one is about public ones.
phrases.notes: The ברייתא is about hidden נגעים, and רבי יוחנן is about visible ones.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי בָּעֵית אֵימָא: הָא בְּצִנְעָא, הָא בְּפַרְהֶסְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a third, independent answer to the challenge of Step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing by the type of case: hidden versus visible
steps.terutzHavaAmina: All נגעים seemed to be the same, so the ברייתא and רבי יוחנן seemed to disagree.
steps.terutzMaskana: Hidden נגעים can be יסורין של אהבה. Visible נגעים, which push people away, are not.

steps.title: How can losing children not be suffering of love?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן's claim that suffering through children is not יסורין של אהבה. If he means children who died, that clashes with his own words about the bone of his tenth son.
steps.simpleTranslation: And suffering through children is not suffering of love?! What case is this? If you say they had children and the children died, didn't רבי יוחנן himself say, 'This is the bone of my tenth son'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now attacks the second half of רבי יוחנן's rule, the part about children. It points out that his own words seem to say the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן lost ten sons and still spoke about the bone of his tenth son. That shows he treated losing children as meaningful suffering from ה׳. So how could he rule that losing children is not יסורין של אהבה?

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? What are the circumstances?
If you say (offering a possible case, usually to reject it)
But didn't [so-and-so] say? (bringing a contradicting statement)

phrases.english: And children are not [suffering of love]?!
What is the case?
If you say that they had [children] and they died,
but didn't רבי יוחנן say,
'This is the bone of my tenth son'?
phrases.notes: רבי יוחנן himself had lost ten sons, and he still talked about it this way.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבָנִים לָא?! הֵיכִי דָמֵי, אִילֵּימָא דַּהֲווֹ לְהוּ וּמֵתוּ, וְהָא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After resolving the challenge about נגעים, the גמרא turns to the other part of רבי יוחנן's rule: children.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's ruling that suffering through children is not יסורין של אהבה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן's own statement about the bone of his tenth son shows that he treated the death of children as meaningful suffering of love. That contradicts his ruling.

steps.title: Never having children versus children who died
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי יוחנן's rule is about someone who never had children at all. Someone who had children and lost them can still be suffering of love.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this one is about someone who never had children at all, and that one is about someone who had children and they died.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction by splitting the cases. רבי יוחנן's rule covers only a person who never had children.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule 'children are not יסורין של אהבה' now means 'having no children at all is not suffering of love.' A person whose children died, like רבי יוחנן himself, can be going through יסורין של אהבה. That fits his words about the bone of his tenth son.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (rejecting the first idea and giving a new one)
This one ... and that one (splitting two cases apart)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן's rule is about someone who never had children. Losing children who were born can still be יסורין של אהבה.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two cases. Losing children is the case that CAN be suffering of love. Never having children is the case that is NOT.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא הָא — דְּלָא הֲווֹ לֵיהּ כְּלָל.
phrases.english: Rather, this one is where he never had [children] at all.
phrases.notes: 'This one' means רבי יוחנן's rule that children are not suffering of love.

phrases.english: And that one is where he had [children] and they died.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא הָא — דְּלָא הֲווֹ לֵיהּ כְּלָל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 9 by narrowing רבי יוחנן's case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: never having children versus children who died
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוחנן's rule meant that losing children is not יסורין של אהבה.
steps.terutzMaskana: His rule covers only someone who never had children. Losing children can be יסורין של אהבה.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן heals רבי חייא בר אבא
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אבא was sick. רבי יוחנן visited him and asked whether his suffering was dear to him. He said he wanted neither the suffering nor its reward. רבי יוחנן took his hand and stood him up.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבא fell ill. רבי יוחנן went in to visit him and said to him: 'Is your suffering dear to you?' He answered: 'Neither it nor its reward.' רבי יוחנן said: 'Give me your hand.' He gave him his hand, and רבי יוחנן stood him up.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a short story that continues the topic of יסורין. A sick sage refuses suffering, and his teacher heals him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person can welcome suffering in order to get its reward. רבי חייא בר אבא says he does not want the suffering, even if it means giving up the reward. Once he says that, רבי יוחנן heals him by taking his hand.

keyTerms.meaning: Is your suffering dear to you?
He stood him up (he healed him)

phrases.english: רבי חייא בר אבא fell ill.
רבי יוחנן went in to [visit] him.
He said to him: Is your suffering dear to you?

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לֹא הֵן וְלֹא שְׂכָרָן.
phrases.english: He said to him: Neither them nor their reward.
He said to him: Give me your hand.
He gave him his hand, and he stood him up.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא חֲלַשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the discussion of which sufferings are of love to stories about sages facing suffering.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A sage could refuse suffering and its reward, and a visiting sage healed him by taking his hand.

steps.title: רבי חנינא heals רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: The same scene repeats, but now רבי יוחנן is the sick one, and רבי חנינא visits and heals him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן fell ill. רבי חנינא went in to visit him and said to him: 'Is your suffering dear to you?' He answered: 'Neither it nor its reward.' רבי חנינא said: 'Give me your hand.' He gave him his hand, and רבי חנינא stood him up.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a second story that matches the first word for word. This time the healer, רבי יוחנן, is the one who needs healing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story is the same, but the roles have switched. רבי יוחנן, who just healed his student, now needs רבי חנינא to heal him. That sets up the question in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Neither the suffering nor its reward

phrases.english: רבי יוחנן fell ill.
רבי חנינא went in to [visit] him.
He said to him: Is your suffering dear to you?

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לֹא הֵן וְלֹא שְׂכָרָן.
phrases.english: He said to him: Neither them nor their reward.
He said to him: Give me your hand.
He gave him his hand, and he stood him up.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן חֲלַשׁ. עָל לְגַבֵּיהּ רַבִּי חֲנִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A matching story with the roles reversed: the healer from step 11 is now the patient.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן also refused suffering and its reward, and רבי חנינא healed him by taking his hand.

steps.title: Why couldn't רבי יוחנן heal himself?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי יוחנן needed רבי חנינא at all. He could heal others, so why not stand himself up?
steps.simpleTranslation: Why? Let רבי יוחנן stand himself up!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא puts the two stories side by side and asks a sharp question. The answer comes in the next part of the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 11, רבי יוחנן healed רבי חייא בר אבא with his hand. If he had that power, he should have been able to heal himself. So why did he have to wait for רבי חנינא?

phrases.english: Why? Let רבי יוחנן stand himself up!

steps.triggerLanguage: אַמַּאי, לוֹקִים רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן לְנַפְשֵׁיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares the two stories and points out an apparent problem in the second one.
steps.kashyaTarget: The story in which רבי יוחנן needed רבי חנינא to heal him
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן could heal his student, so he should also have been able to heal himself without help.

steps.title: A prisoner cannot free himself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that a person cannot release himself from his own prison. He needs someone else.
steps.simpleTranslation: They say: a prisoner cannot free himself from prison.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 13: why could רבי יוחנן not heal himself? A sick person is like a prisoner, and a prisoner needs someone on the outside to free him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן's power to heal others does not work on himself. Being sick is like being locked up. You cannot open the lock from inside, so even a great healer needs another person.
steps.whatToRemember: A sick person cannot heal himself, just as a prisoner cannot unlock his own prison. He needs help from someone else.

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרִי: אֵין חָבוּשׁ מַתִּיר עַצְמוֹ מִבֵּית הָאֲסוּרִים.
phrases.english: They say: A prisoner does not free himself from prison.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי: אֵין חָבוּשׁ מַתִּיר עַצְמוֹ מִבֵּית הָאֲסוּרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question of Step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: General principle: a healer cannot heal himself
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If רבי יוחנן could heal others, he should have been able to heal himself.
steps.terutzMaskana: A sick person is like a prisoner and cannot free himself. He needs someone else.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן visits sick רבי אלעזר and lights up the room
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר is sick and lying in a dark room. רבי יוחנן visits and uncovers his arm, and light fills the room.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר became sick. רבי יוחנן came in to visit him. He saw that he was lying in a dark room. He uncovered his arm, and light fell across the room.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new story about a sick visit, like the ones in Steps 11–12. This step sets the scene for the conversation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a third story in the same pattern: a sick student and a visiting teacher. The detail about the light from רבי יוחנן's arm matters later, because his beauty is what רבי אלעזר will cry over.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar became sick.
Rabbi Yoḥanan went in to visit him.

phrases.aramaic: חֲזָא דַּהֲוָה קָא גָּנֵי בְּבֵית אָפֵל.
phrases.english: He saw that he was lying in a dark room.
He uncovered his arm, and light fell across the room.
phrases.notes: The light came from רבי יוחנן's own skin. This is the beauty that comes up again in Step 17.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר חֲלַשׁ. עַל לְגַבֵּיהּ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a third sick-visit story in the same pattern as Steps 11–12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Story setup: רבי אלעזר is sick in a dark room, and רבי יוחנן brings light by uncovering his arm.

steps.title: Why are you crying? Three possible comforts
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן sees רבי אלעזר crying, asks why, and offers comfort for three possible reasons: too little תורה, not enough money, or children who died.
steps.simpleTranslation: He saw that רבי אלעזר was crying. He said to him: Why are you crying? If it is because of תורה that you did not learn enough of, we learned: one who does a lot and one who does a little are the same, as long as he directs his heart to Heaven. If it is because of food and money, not every person gets to have two tables. If it is because of children, this is the bone of my tenth son.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן asks רבי אלעזר why he is crying. Before he answers, רבי יוחנן guesses three possible reasons and comforts him about each one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each comfort answers a different kind of pain. For תורה: what counts is the intention for Heaven, not the amount. For money: not everyone gets both wealth and תורה. For children: רבי יוחנן himself lost ten sons, which ties back to Steps 9–10, where losing children can still be suffering of love.

keyTerms.meaning: One who does a lot and one who does a little (are equal)
That he directs his heart toward Heaven

phrases.aramaic: חַזְיֵיהּ דַּהֲוָה קָא בָּכֵי רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר.
phrases.english: He saw that Rabbi Elazar was crying.
He said to him: Why are you crying?
If it is because of Torah that you did not learn much of —
We learned: One who brings a lot and one who brings a little are the same,
phrases.notes: This line is from a משנה about קרבנות. A big offering and a small one are worth the same if the heart is right.

phrases.english: As long as he directs his heart toward Heaven.
And if it is because of food and money —

phrases.aramaic: לֹא כׇּל אָדָם זוֹכֶה לִשְׁתֵּי שֻׁלְחָנוֹת.
phrases.english: Not every person merits two tables.
And if it is because of children —
This is the bone of my tenth son.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אַמַּאי קָא בָּכֵית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story. רבי יוחנן now sees the tears and asks about them.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רבי אלעזר is crying. רבי יוחנן offers three guesses with a comfort for each.

steps.title: Crying over beauty that will rot in the ground
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר says he is crying over רבי יוחנן's beauty, which will one day decay in the earth. רבי יוחנן agrees that this is worth crying over, and they both cry.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I am crying over this beauty that will rot in the dust. He said to him: Over this you are surely right to cry. And they both cried.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר answers the question. None of the three guesses was right. He is crying because even beauty like רבי יוחנן's will end in the grave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן's comforts were about רבי אלעזר's own troubles, but רבי אלעזר is thinking about death, which comes to everyone. רבי יוחנן does not argue with this. He agrees, and they cry together.

keyTerms.meaning: That will rot in the dust

phrases.english: He said to him: Over this beauty
phrases.notes: He means רבי יוחנן's beauty, the beauty whose light just filled the room.

phrases.english: That will rot in the dust, I am crying.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: עַל דָּא וַדַּאי קָא בָּכֵית,
phrases.english: He said to him: Over this you are surely right to cry,
And they both cried.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְהַאי שׁוּפְרָא דְּבָלֵי בְּעַפְרָא קָא בָּכֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 16 and sets aside all three of רבי יוחנן's guesses.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He is crying over רבי יוחנן's beauty, which will decay in the grave, not over his own troubles.

steps.title: Neither the suffering nor its reward, and רבי יוחנן stands him up
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן asks whether the suffering is dear to him. רבי אלעזר says he wants neither the suffering nor its reward, so רבי יוחנן takes his hand and stands him up.
steps.simpleTranslation: Meanwhile, he said to him: Is your suffering dear to you? He said to him: Neither it nor its reward. He said to him: Give me your hand. He gave him his hand, and he stood him up.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends with the same pattern as Steps 11–12. רבי אלעזר does not want the suffering, so רבי יוחנן heals him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'neither it nor its reward' shows he is not accepting the suffering willingly. So רבי יוחנן, as the person from the outside, frees the 'prisoner' from Step 14 by taking his hand and raising him up.

keyTerms.meaning: Meanwhile, in the middle of all this
And he stood him up (healed him)

steps.whatToRemember: All three stories end the same way. The sick person does not want suffering or its reward, and someone else heals him by taking his hand, because a prisoner cannot free himself.

phrases.english: Meanwhile, he said to him:
Is your suffering dear to you?

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לֹא הֵן וְלֹא שְׂכָרָן.
phrases.english: He said to him: Neither it nor its reward.
He said to him: Give me your hand,
He gave him his hand, and he stood him up.

steps.triggerLanguage: חֲבִיבִין עָלֶיךָ יִסּוּרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the רבי אלעזר story with the same healing exchange seen in Steps 11–12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אלעזר does not want the suffering or its reward, and רבי יוחנן heals him by taking his hand.

steps.title: רב הונא's wine turns sour and the Sages tell him to examine his deeds
steps.stepSummary: Four hundred barrels of רב הונא's wine turn into vinegar. רב יהודה (or רב אדא בר אהבה) and the חכמים visit him and tell him to examine his actions.
steps.simpleTranslation: Four hundred barrels of רב הונא's wine went sour. רב יהודה, the brother of רב סלא חסידא, came to him with the חכמים. Some say it was רב אדא בר אהבה with the חכמים. They said to him: 'Let the master look into his deeds.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new story about suffering. רב הונא has a big financial loss, and his visitors tell him to check his actions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This story connects to the earlier idea that when suffering comes, a person should look into his deeds. Here the 'suffering' is a loss of money, not illness. The visitors are not comforting him. They are pushing him to find what went wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: turned sour, went bad (said of wine becoming vinegar)
let the master examine his deeds

phrases.english: Rav Huna had go sour on him
four hundred barrels of wine.
Rav Yehuda went in to him,
the brother of Rav Sala the Pious, together with the Sages,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה וְרַבָּנַן,
phrases.english: and some say it was Rav Adda bar Ahava together with the Sages,
and they said to him: Let the master examine his deeds.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב הוּנָא תְּקִיפוּ לֵיהּ אַרְבַּע מְאָה דַּנֵּי דְחַמְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the story of רבי יוחנן and רבי אלעזר, the גמרא brings a new story about suffering, this time a loss of money.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When a loss comes, a person should examine his deeds.

steps.title: רב הונא protests: do you suspect me of doing wrong?
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא pushes back and asks whether they consider him suspected of sin.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said to them: 'Am I suspected in your eyes?'
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא objects to the advice. He is asking whether they really think he did something wrong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It looks like a question, but it works as a challenge. רב הונא is saying he has no known sin, so why tell him to search his deeds? This sets up the חכמים' reply.

phrases.english: He said to them: And am I suspected in your eyes?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי חֲשִׁידְנָא בְּעֵינַיְיכוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pushes back against the advice to examine his deeds.
steps.kashyaTarget: The visitors' advice that רב הונא should examine his deeds.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Telling someone to search his deeds implies he sinned, and רב הונא does not see himself as someone suspected of sin.

steps.title: The Sages answer that God does not punish without justice
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים reply: Is קודשא בריך הוא suspected of judging without justice? There must be a reason for the loss.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: 'Is the Holy One, Blessed be He, suspected of giving a judgment without justice?'
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים answer רב הונא's protest by turning his question around.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא asked, 'Am I suspected?' They answer, 'Is ה' suspected?' One of you has to be wrong. Since ה' never punishes unfairly, the loss must have a cause, so רב הונא should look for it.

keyTerms.meaning: the Holy One, Blessed be He
judgment without justice (punishment for no reason)

steps.whatToRemember: A punishment from ה' is never without a reason. That is why a person who suffers a loss should check his deeds.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ: מִי חֲשִׁיד קוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא
phrases.english: They said to him: Is the Holy One, Blessed be He, suspected
of carrying out judgment without justice?!

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי חֲשִׁיד קוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא דְּעָבֵיד דִּינָא בְּלָא דִּינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב הונא's protest.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Turning the question around: the alternative to suspecting him is suspecting ה', which is impossible.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב הונא thought he had done nothing wrong, so the advice was insulting.
steps.terutzMaskana: Since ה' judges fairly, there must be something in רב הונא's conduct to fix.

steps.title: רב הונא asks them to say what they have heard
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא invites anyone who has heard something bad about him to say it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: 'If anyone has heard something about me, let him say it.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא accepts their point and now asks what exactly he did wrong. This sets up the next step, where they tell him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His tone has changed from protest to openness. He is now willing to hear about his own fault.

keyTerms.meaning: who has heard something about me

phrases.english: He said to them: If there is anyone
who has heard something about me, let him say it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי אִיכָּא מַאן דִּשְׁמִיעַ עֲלַי מִלְּתָא לֵימָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After accepting that there must be a reason, רב הונא asks what it is.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What wrongdoing have people heard about רב הונא?

steps.title: The Sages reveal that he does not give his sharecropper the vine branches
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים say they heard that רב הונא does not give his אריס his share of the שבישא (vine branches).
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: 'This is what we heard: that the master does not give the vine branches to his sharecropper.'
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים name the wrong they heard about: רב הונא was holding back what his sharecropper was owed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אריס works the owner's field in exchange for a share of what grows. The vine branches were part of what he should get, and רב הונא was keeping them.

keyTerms.meaning: vine branches, the cuttings of the vine
sharecropper who works a field for a share of the crop

phrases.english: They said to him: This is what we heard,
that the master does not give the vine branches to his sharecropper.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי שְׁמִיעַ לָן דְּלָא יָהֵיב מָר שְׁבִישָׁא לַאֲרִיסֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב הונא's request to hear what he did wrong.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He withholds the vine branches owed to his sharecropper.

steps.title: רב הונא defends himself: the sharecropper steals everything
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא explains that the sharecropper leaves him nothing and steals it all, so keeping the branches is just getting back what is his.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: 'Does he leave me anything of it? He steals all of it!'
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא defends his behavior. He says he is only making up for what the sharecropper already stole from him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He does not deny keeping the branches. He argues it is fair, because the sharecropper took far more from him. This defense sets up the חכמים' final answer.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ: מִי קָא שָׁבֵיק לִי מִידֵּי מִינֵּיהּ?
phrases.english: He said to them: Does he leave me anything of it?
Why, he steals all of it!

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי קָא שָׁבֵיק לִי מִידֵּי מִינֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends against the accusation in step 23.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Justification: he says he is recovering what was stolen from him.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Withholding the branches looks like cheating the sharecropper.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב הונא claims it is fair payback, since the sharecropper steals everything.

steps.title: The Sages reject this: stealing from a thief still tastes of theft
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים quote a folk saying: one who steals after a thief also tastes the taste of theft.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: 'This is what people say: Steal after a thief, and you taste the taste of theft.'
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים push away רב הונא's defense with a well-known folk saying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if the sharecropper is a thief, taking back on your own still has a flavor of theft. Being wronged does not make it fully clean to help yourself. For someone on רב הונא's level, even this was enough to bring a loss.

keyTerms.meaning: this is what people say (a folk saying)

steps.whatToRemember: Taking back from someone who wronged you, on your own, still has a taste of theft.
steps.confusionAlert: The saying does not mean רב הונא is a full thief. It means his action has a 'taste' of theft, which was enough to be held against someone of his stature.

phrases.english: They said to him: This is what people say:
"Steal after a thief, and you taste the taste" of theft.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַיְינוּ דְאָמְרִי אִינָשֵׁי בָּתַר גַּנָּבָא גְּנוֹב וְטַעְמָא טְעֵים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב הונא's defense from step 24.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the idea that recovering stolen property on your own is completely innocent.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Even taking back from a thief carries a taste of theft.

steps.title: רב הונא commits to paying and his loss is restored
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא accepts upon himself to give the sharecropper his share. Then his loss is reversed: either the vinegar became wine again, or vinegar became as expensive as wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: 'I take it upon myself to give it to him.' Some say the vinegar turned back into wine. Others say the price of vinegar went up, and it was sold for the price of wine.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends: רב הונא fixes his ways, and his money is given back to him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once he committed to pay what he owed, the loss was undone. The two versions differ only in how: by a miracle (vinegar became wine) or through the market (vinegar sold at wine prices). Either way, his repentance brought the loss back.
steps.whatToRemember: Once רב הונא corrected his behavior, his loss was restored. Checking your deeds and fixing them can reverse a punishment.
steps.whyThisMatters: This story shows the full path in action: a loss, checking one's deeds, finding the fault, fixing it, and having the loss reversed.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ: קַבֵּילְנָא עָלַי דְּיָהֵיבְנָא לֵיהּ.
phrases.english: He said to them: I take it upon myself that I will give it to him.

phrases.aramaic: אִיכָּא דְאָמְרִי: הֲדַר חַלָּא וַהֲוָה חַמְרָא.
phrases.english: Some say: The vinegar turned back and became wine.
And some say: The price of vinegar went up,
and it was sold at the price of wine.

steps.triggerLanguage: קַבֵּילְנָא עָלַי דְּיָהֵיבְנָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רב הונא accepts the rebuke from step 25 and the story ends with his loss restored.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: After רב הונא committed to give the sharecropper his share, his loss of wine was made up, either by miracle or by the price of vinegar rising.

steps.title: אבא בנימין's two lifelong concerns
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes אבא בנימין: all his life he took care that his תפלה be "before his bed" and that his bed be placed between north and south.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: אבא בנימין says, all my life I worked hard on two things. That my prayer should be before my bed, and that my bed should be placed between north and south.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא in which אבא בנימין lists two things he always made sure to do. This sets up the next steps, which explain each of the two things.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gives two practices but does not explain either one. The rest of this section works through them one at a time: first the prayer, then the bed.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא whose name is quoted here
Took pains, was careful and concerned about

phrases.english: It was taught: Abba Binyamin says:

phrases.aramaic: עַל שְׁנֵי דְבָרִים הָיִיתִי מִצְטַעֵר כׇּל יָמַי —
phrases.english: About two things I took great pains all my days:
about my prayer, that it should be before my bed,

phrases.aramaic: וְעַל מִטָּתִי שֶׁתְּהֵא נְתוּנָה בֵּין צָפוֹן לְדָרוֹם.
phrases.english: and about my bed, that it should be placed between north and south.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא אַבָּא בִּנְיָמִין אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic about תפלה and sleep, after the story of רב הונא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אבא בנימין was careful that his תפלה be "before his bed" and that his bed face between north and south.

steps.title: What does "before my bed" mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the first half of אבא בנימין's statement and asks what "before my bed" means.
steps.simpleTranslation: "That my prayer should be before my bed": what does "before my bed" mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops on the first practice and asks for the meaning of the words "before my bed."
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase is unclear. It could describe where he stood, or it could mean something else. The question sets up a test of the simple reading in the next step.

phrases.english: "About my prayer, that it should be before my bed":
what does "before my bed" mean?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי לִפְנֵי מִטָּתִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of the first practice in step 27.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the phrase "before my bed."

steps.title: Praying literally in front of the bed is a problem
steps.stepSummary: If "before my bed" means literally standing in front of the bed, that clashes with the rule that nothing should separate the one praying from the wall. The rule is learned from חזקיהו turning to the wall.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it literally means in front of my bed, there is a problem. רב יהודה said in the name of רב, and some say in the name of רבי יהושע בן לוי: From where do we know that one who prays should have nothing between him and the wall? As it says, "And חזקיהו turned his face to the wall and prayed."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the simple reading, that he stood in front of his bed to pray, and attacks it with a known rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a rule that a person praying should not have anything between himself and the wall. A bed in front of him would be exactly such a thing in between. So the literal reading cannot be right.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (introduces a reading that will be rejected)
King חזקיהו, who turned to the wall to pray

phrases.english: If you say it means literally "in front of my bed,"
but Rav Yehuda said that Rav said,
and some say it was Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi:
From where do we know that one who prays

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלֹּא יְהֵא דָּבָר חוֹצֵץ בֵּינוֹ לְבֵין הַקִּיר —
phrases.english: should have nothing separating between him and the wall?
As it says: "And Chizkiyahu turned his face
to the wall and prayed"?
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 38:2

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵּימָא לִפְנֵי מִטָּתִי מַמָּשׁ וְהָאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests a literal answer to the question in step 28 and rejects it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The literal reading that אבא בנימין stood in front of his bed to pray.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A bed in front of the one praying would separate him from the wall, which goes against the rule learned from חזקיהו.

steps.title: Read it as "close to my bed"
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא changes the reading: not "before my bed" but "close to my bed."
steps.simpleTranslation: Don't say "before my bed." Rather, say "close to my bed."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the problem by reading the phrase differently, as "close to my bed."
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the words mean "close to" instead of "in front of," there is no longer a bed standing between him and the wall. As for time, רש״י explains it as davening right after he got up from bed, before doing any work or learning תורה.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather say (read it this other way)

steps.whatToRemember: "Before my bed" does not mean standing in front of the bed. "Close to my bed" is about time: davening right after getting up, before starting work. So the bed is not standing between the one praying and the wall.

phrases.english: Do not say "before my bed,"
rather say "close to my bed."

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא תֵּימָא לִפְנֵי מִטָּתִי אֶלָּא אֵימָא סָמוּךְ לְמִטָּתִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the problem in step 29 by re-reading the phrase.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: "Before my bed" means physically standing in front of the bed.
steps.terutzMaskana: "Close to my bed" means close in time, davening right after rising, so the rule about the wall is kept.

steps.title: A bed between north and south brings male children
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns to the second practice. רבי חמא ברבי חנינא, quoting רבי יצחק, says that whoever places his bed between north and south will have sons, based on a פסוק in תהלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: "And that my bed should be placed between north and south." As רבי חמא ברבי חנינא said that רבי יצחק said: anyone who places his bed between north and south will have male children, as it says, "And with Your treasure You fill their belly; they will be satisfied with sons."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the second half of אבא בנימין's statement. It then explains why that practice is worthwhile.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word for "Your treasure," צפונך, sounds like צפון, "north." The same פסוק goes on to mention sons. So a bed placed toward the north is linked to having male children.

keyTerms.meaning: And (with) Your treasure; sounds like צפון

phrases.aramaic: ״וְעַל מִטָּתִי שֶׁתְּהֵא נְתוּנָה בֵּין צָפוֹן לַדָּרוֹם״.
phrases.english: "And about my bed, that it should be placed between north and south."

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי חָמָא בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא, אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק:
phrases.english: As Rabbi Chama son of Rabbi Chanina said that Rabbi Yitzchak said:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל הַנּוֹתֵן מִטָּתוֹ בֵּין צָפוֹן לְדָרוֹם
phrases.english: Anyone who places his bed between north and south
will have male children,
as it says: "And with Your treasure You fill their belly;
they will be satisfied with sons."
phrases.notes: תהלים 17:14. "Your treasure" (צפונך) sounds like צפון, north, and that is the hook.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי חָמָא בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the first practice (prayer) to the second practice (the bed) in step 27.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Placing one's bed between north and south brings male children.

steps.title: His wife will also not miscarry
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק adds another reward: the wife will not miscarry. He learns it by linking "fill their belly" to רבקה's pregnancy, where "her days were filled" and twins were in her belly.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: also, his wife will not miscarry. It is written here, "And with Your treasure You fill their belly," and it is written there, "And her days to give birth were filled, and behold, there were twins in her belly."
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק adds a second reward for placing the bed between north and south, and shows where he learns it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both פסוקים use the words "fill" and "belly." In רבקה's case the pregnancy was "filled," meaning it went to full term. So "You fill their belly" also means a full pregnancy with no miscarriage.
steps.whatToRemember: A bed between north and south brings two rewards: male children (רבי יצחק) and no miscarriage (רב נחמן בר יצחק). Both are learned from the same פסוק in תהלים: the first from צפונך, and the second from "fill their belly."

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
Also, his wife will not miscarry.
It is written here: "And with Your treasure You fill their belly,"
and it is written there: "And her days to give birth were filled,
and behold, there were twins in her belly."
phrases.notes: בראשית 25:24, about רבקה. The shared words "fill" and "belly" link the two פסוקים.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק אָמַר אַף אֵין אִשְׁתּוֹ מַפֶּלֶת נְפָלִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second reward to the one given in step 31, using the same פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One whose bed is between north and south: his wife will not miscarry, learned by linking the פסוק in תהלים to רבקה's full-term pregnancy.

steps.title: Leaving your friend alone while he prays
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes אבא בנימין: if two people come to pray and one finishes first and leaves without waiting for the other, his own תפלה is torn up before him. The source is a פסוק in איוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: אבא בנימין says: Two people went in to pray. One of them finished praying first, did not wait for his friend, and left. His prayer is torn up in front of his face, as the פסוק says: 'You who tear your soul in your face, is the earth to be abandoned for your sake?'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching from אבא בנימין. He warns that if someone leaves his friend alone in the middle of praying, his own תפלה is thrown back at him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a new topic, not part of the bed discussion from earlier, but it comes from the same speaker, אבא בנימין. The punishment matches the wrong: he hurt his friend's prayer, so his own prayer is ruined. The proof is the word 'טֹרֵף' (tearing) in the פסוק, which he reads as 'tearing up' the person's prayer.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא whose teachings about prayer the גמרא has been quoting

phrases.english: It was taught: Abba Binyamin says:
Two people who went in to pray,
and one of them finished praying first,
and did not wait for his friend, and left,
his prayer is torn up in front of his face,
as it says: 'He tears his soul in his face,'
phrases.notes: איוב 18:4. Here באפו is read as 'in his face,' which matches 'torn up in front of his face.'

phrases.english: 'is the earth to be abandoned for your sake?'

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא. אַבָּא בִּנְיָמִין אוֹמֵר: שְׁנַיִם שֶׁנִּכְנְסוּ לְהִתְפַּלֵּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of where the bed is placed and brings a different teaching from the same speaker, אבא בנימין, whose statement was quoted in step 27.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who finishes praying and leaves his friend alone has his own prayer torn up before him, learned from 'טֹרֵף נַפְשׁוֹ בְּאַפּוֹ' (איוב 18:4).

steps.title: He also makes the שכינה leave ישראל
steps.stepSummary: אבא בנימין adds that this person also causes the שכינה to leave ישראל. He learns it from the end of the same פסוק, 'the צור is moved from its place,' and proves that צור means הקדוש ברוך הוא from a פסוק in דברים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And not only that, but he causes the שכינה to leave ישראל, as it says: 'And the Rock is moved from its place.' And 'Rock' means only הקדוש ברוך הוא, as it says: 'The Rock that gave birth to you, you forgot.'
steps.whatsHappening: אבא בנימין adds a second, bigger result of leaving a friend alone. The person also makes the שכינה leave ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof comes from the end of the same פסוק in איוב: 'the צור is moved from its place.' To show that 'צור' here means ה׳ and not a real rock, he brings a פסוק in דברים where ה׳ is called 'צור.' So the harm goes beyond his own prayer and affects all of ישראל.

keyTerms.meaning: And not only that, but also
Rock; here, a name for ה׳
The Holy One, Blessed be He

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read 'צור' as a real rock moving. אבא בנימין proves from דברים that 'צור' is a name for ה׳, so 'the צור is moved' means the שכינה leaves.
steps.whatToRemember: Leaving a friend alone in the middle of תפלה ruins your own prayer, and it also causes the שכינה to leave ישראל. Both come from one פסוק in איוב.

phrases.english: And not only that, but he causes
the Divine Presence to leave Israel,
as it says: 'And the Rock is moved from its place.'
phrases.notes: This is the end of the same פסוק, איוב 18:4.

phrases.english: And 'Rock' means only the Holy One, Blessed be He,
as it says: 'The Rock that gave birth to you, you forgot.'
phrases.notes: דברים 32:18

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֹא עוֹד, אֶלָּא שֶׁגּוֹרֵם לַשְּׁכִינָה שֶׁתִּסְתַּלֵּק מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues אבא בנימין's statement, adding a second result taken from the end of the same פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who leaves his friend praying alone causes the שכינה to leave ישראל, since 'צור' in איוב 18:4 refers to הקדוש ברוך הוא (דברים 32:18).

steps.title: What is the reward for waiting?
steps.stepSummary: After hearing the punishment for leaving, the גמרא asks the other side: what reward does someone get if he waits for his friend?
steps.simpleTranslation: And if he waits for him, what is his reward?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks the opposite question: if leaving brings punishment, what does a person gain by waiting? This line sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We just learned the punishment for leaving. Now the גמרא wants to know the good side of the same act. The answer is not given on this amud; it comes at the start of the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: And if he waited for him

phrases.english: And if he waited for him, what is his reward?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם הִמְתִּין לוֹ מַה שְּׂכָרוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the punishment for leaving (steps 33-34) to ask about the reward for waiting.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What reward a person receives for waiting for his friend to finish praying, as the opposite of the punishment just described.
